title: Georgia Privilege Confidentiality Subsection Outline
goal: Develop a citation-supported outline for a subsection of a memorandum on the attorney-client privilege in Georgia, addressing the confidentiality requirement and the effect of internal organizational participants or third parties on a communication.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: The session produced a substantial, citation-supported draft of the confidentiality foundation, but it did not produce the planned compact, verified outline. The participant-specific analysis was deferred to later subsections, and several pinpoint citations remain to be completed.

Step 1 + Step 2 + Step 3 + Step 4.step_name: Step 1: Frame the limited confidentiality issue / Step 2: Identify a small set of core authorities / Step 3: Extract the governing rules and exceptions / Step 4: Assemble the subsection outline
Step 1 + Step 2 + Step 3 + Step 4.step_action:
Step 1: I will explain that the task is limited to outlining how Georgia law determines whether a communication remained confidential when shared within an organization or with a third party. I will exclude the privilege's other elements and broader waiver doctrines except where they are necessary to explain this issue.

Step 2: I will use Claude and Lexis Plus to locate the leading Georgia authorities on confidentiality, internal organizational communications, and third-party participation. I will limit the research set to the statute and approximately three to five decisions that directly support the necessary rule statements.

Step 3: I will distill the selected authorities into rules addressing intent to maintain confidentiality, communications among organizational representatives, and participation by agents or other third parties. I will distinguish necessary participants from unrelated outsiders without expanding into a comprehensive waiver analysis.

Step 4: I will organize the rules under no more than three substantive subheadings: the confidentiality requirement, internal organizational communications, and third-party participation. I will place the best authority and a concise parenthetical beneath each rule rather than drafting full memorandum prose.

nodes.label: State the goal and submit the combined framing-and-research request
nodes.detail: Types and submits a single message stating the session's goal (a citation-supported outline on confidentiality plus the effect of internal-organizational and third-party participants) and asking Claude to prepare a basic outline with case excerpts for review -- this one message also carries the Step 2-4 research/outline ask.

nodes.label: Research Georgia authorities and generate the citation-supported outline
nodes.detail: Runs a dozen-plus targeted web searches (the statute, third-party-presence case law, St. Simons Waterfront, Marriott, Atlantic Coast Line, the common-interest doctrine, and the most recent Georgia authority) fetching primary sources rather than relying on memory, then distills that research directly into rule statements and delivers the full outline in one response: Part A (confidentiality as an independent threshold element), Part B (third-party presence defeating confidentiality), Part C (necessary participants who do not destroy it), Part D (internal organizational participants and the Marriott five-factor test), and Part E (synthesis), plus a list of five open items to run down before filing.

nodes.label: Read through the delivered outline
nodes.detail: Reviews the five-part outline and its citations silently -- no further chat activity occurs in this window before he asks about an unfamiliar term in one of the cited cases.

nodes.label: Submit the amanuensis vocabulary question
nodes.detail: Asks Claude what the term 'amanuensis' means, as used in the Taylor v. Taylor citation in the outline.

nodes.label: Define the term and tie it to the outline's authority
nodes.detail: Explains the word's Latin origin and modern equivalent (legal secretary/transcriptionist), then connects it back to the staff, paralegal, and investigator authority already cited in the outline (Martinez, In re Stoutamire, In re Fulton County Grand Jury Proceedings).

nodes.label: Read the explanation and decide what to draft next
nodes.detail: Absorbs the clarification before deciding to have Claude draft the first subsection (Part A) in full prose.

Step 4.step_action: I will organize the rules under no more than three substantive subheadings: the confidentiality requirement, internal organizational communications, and third-party participation. I will place the best authority and a concise parenthetical beneath each rule rather than drafting full memorandum prose.

nodes.label: Submit the request to draft sections 5 through 8
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to draft sections 5 through 8 of Part A, extending the revised draft with the remaining rule statements.

nodes.label: Verify the file state, then draft the remaining sections
nodes.detail: First checks whether the uploaded draft differs from the version last reviewed to avoid drafting against a stale copy, then delivers sections 5-8 (intended audience, non-conferral of confidentiality, scope of protection) in the established voice and citation style, with verification notes on citations sourced from a compendium rather than the opinions themselves.

nodes.label: Incorporate the new sections before the next audit
nodes.detail: Reviews and pastes the newly drafted sections 5-8 into the working document in Word.

Step 5.step_action: I will confirm the citations and pinpoint references, remove duplicative or tangential material, and flag any proposition that requires later research. I will stop at a fleshed-out outline and reserve drafting for a later time.

nodes.label: Submit the request for a clean, error-corrected version
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to proofread, revise, and refine the full draft, fixing everything previously flagged, and to give clean text he can paste in directly.

nodes.label: Fix everything fixable while flagging what it cannot verify
nodes.detail: Corrects citation-format and drafting errors throughout the draft, but refuses to fabricate pinpoint citations it cannot confirm, leaving explicit [pin] placeholders in their place instead.

nodes.label: Incorporate the corrected draft
nodes.detail: Pastes the corrected text into the working document, then modifies it.

nodes.label: Ask Claude whether issues remain
nodes.detail: Asks Claude whether any issues remain, telling it to set aside the still-open [pin] placeholders.

nodes.label: Surface a final round of errors and one unsupported claim
nodes.detail: Catalogs a heading-capitalization slip, an inconsistent citation short-form, a broken cross-reference, and one proposition asserted without supporting authority.

nodes.label: Review the final flagged items and close the session
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's last list of issues and switches to the working Word document for a final read-through; per the workflow document, the pinpoint citations and the internal-participant/third-party sections remain unfinished when the session ends.
